items.title: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework
items.teaser: The Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada jointly review and renew the Bank’s monetary policy framework every five years. The Bank then independently conducts monetary policy to achieve the framework’s goals. The Government and the Bank agree that monetary policy must work to promote the economic and financial well being of Canadians. We also agree that the best way monetary policy can do this is by keeping inflation low, stable, and predictable, thereby protecting Canadians from large increases in the cost of living. A credible and well understood monetary policy framework that focuses on price stability helps the economy grow, supports investment and job creation, and fosters confidence in Canada’s economy.

items.title: Building a stronger Canada through a well-managed, predictable immigration system

Last year and through Budget 2025, we committed to taking back control over the immigration system and putting Canada on a trajectory to bring immigration back to sustainable levels.

items.title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Sudbury
items.teaser: Today, the Governments of Canada and Ontario announced that the City of Greater Sudbury is receiving up to $45.3 million through the Development Charge Reduction Program (DCRP) in recognition of its commitment to reduce development charges by 100 per cent for residential developments from March 30, 2026 to March 31, 2029. The funding will help build more homes and community infrastructure in Sudbury while advancing the province’s plan to protect Ontario by investing in projects that support economic growth and keep workers on the job.

items.title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Essex County

items.title: Government of Canada will be accepting applications for $5,000 Team Canada Strong Red Seal Completion Bonus as of November 16

items.title: Backgrounder : Team Canada Strong
items.teaser: Team Canada Strong is an $8 billion investment to recruit, train, and hire 80,000 to 100,000 new Red Seal skilled trades workers by 2030-2031. It includes a $2 billion federal investment to help support PT workforce development efforts to better align skills development with local labour market needs and grow apprenticeship opportunities across Canada.

items.title: Government of Canada provides an update the 2026 wildfire season – October update
items.teaser: Wildfire seasons are now longer, more complex and more challenging than in the past, and 2026 was no exception. After a slower than average start to the season, wildfire activity, driven by periods of prolonged heat, drought and low humidity, became significant in several regions across the country. Northwestern Ontario and Southern British Columbia were particularly affected, experiencing sustained wildfire activity that threatened communities and critical infrastructure. Wildfire activity was also extremely intense in the Northwest Territories, which accounted for over one third of the total area burned in Canada in 2026.

items.title: Safe and effective health products for Canadians: New authorizations between July and September 2026

items.title: Drugs and medical devices authorized, July 1 to September 30, 2026
items.teaser: From July 1 to September 30, 2026, Health Canada approved 16 new drug submissions (14 pharmaceuticals, 2 biologics) and 540 new medical devices, including 27 Class IV medical devices, which present the greatest potential risk. During this period, Health Canada also approved 30 generic drugs and 3 biosimilar drugs.
